item.title: Your chance to train with GM Harshit Raja at the new ChessBase India office
item.description: Grandmaster Harshit Raja is coming to Mumbai. From 17th to 19th August 2026, the 2504-rated GM will conduct two intensive camps at ChessBase India's new Vidyavihar office - mornings on the secrets of positional chess for beginners, evenings on calculation for players rated 1800 and above. Both groups are kept small, so this is closer to private training than a lecture. Registration is open now, and seats are limited.

item.title: Story of India's 96th Grandmaster Ethan Vaz
item.description: Fourteen-year-old Ethan Vaz landed in Mumbai still riding high from a life-changing trip across Europe. In just a few whirlwind weeks, the young Goan chess player won the Sarajevo GM Mix in Bosnia and Herzegovina, secured his final Grandmaster norm, and becameIndia's 96th Grandmaster. Hardly stopping to celebrate, he kept the momentum going, capping off his trip with a third-place finish at the Serbia Open Masters.

item.title: How did 14-year-old Deekshitha Modipalli reached 2400+ from 1985 in just two months
item.description: Every once in a while, a young player comes along whose rise is hard to ignore. The most recent one is 14-year-old Deekshitha Modipalli, who, in just two months, gained nearly 450 Elo points, crossed the 2400 mark, and picked up an IM norm along the way. This talented girl has been travelling independently to chess tournaments since she was just 10 years old. Let's take a look at her incredible run!

item.title: Sinquefield Cup 2026 R3: Wesley So Beats Caruana Fabiano to Gain Sole Lead
item.description: In the 3rd round of the Sinquefield Cup 2026, there were 3 decisive results. Praggnanandhaa lost to Vincent Keymer with black pieces. Sam Sevian defeated Anish Giri, and Wesley So defeated Fabiano Caruana to gain the sole lead. The games between Javokhir Sindarov vs. Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and Jorden van Foreest vs. Levon Aronian ended in a draw. The 4th round will start on 13th August at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photos: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Cairns Cup 2026 R3: Divya Deshmukh Beats Former World Champion Alexandra Kosteniuk
item.description: In the 3rd round of the Cairns Cup 2026, Divya Deshmukh defeated former Women's World Champion Alexandra Kosteniuk with black pieces. Divya secured an early opening advantage in a closed Sicilian Defence and converted it smoothly with black pieces. It was the only decisive result of the round, and now Divya is in second place with 2/3 points. The 4th round will start on 13th August at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photos: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Praggnanandhaa Takes Down World Championship Challenger Javokhir Sindarov
item.description: R. Praggnanandhaa scored a big win against World Championship Challenger Javokhir Sindarov in the 2nd round of the Sinquefield Cup 2026. Praggnanandhaa was pressing in the Rook Knight endgame, and eventually Sindarov made a mistake, and Pragg won the 6-hour-long marathon game in 95 moves. There were 3 more decisive results where Aronian won against Vincent Keymer, MVL won against Sam Sevian, and Wesley So defeated Jorden van Foreest. The 3rd round will start on 12th August at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photos: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Cairns Cup 2026 R2: Alice Lee and Tan Zhongyi Score 2nd Consecutive Win
item.description: Tan Zhongyi and Alice Lee scored their second consecutive wins at the Cairns Cup 2026. In the 2nd round, Tan Zhongyi defeated Koneru Humpy with the white pieces, and Alice Lee defeated Divya Deshmukh with black. In another decisive result, Carissa Yip won against Alexandra Kosteniuk. The Game between Bibisara Assaubayeva and Vaishali ended in a draw. The 3rd round will start on 12th August at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photos: Lennart Ootes

item.title: EWC Chess 2026 Day 1: Andrey Esipenko and Wei Yi Qualify for Group Stage, Aravindh's Run is Over
item.description: The Esports World Cup (EWC) Chess Tournament kicks off at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles. The Opening Day saw 8 players fighting hard in Play-Ins for the final 2 spots in the Group Stages. Wei Yi of Team Nemesis and Andrey Esipenko of Team Virtus.Pro made their way to the final 16 and will compete in the Group Stages on 12th August. Wei Yi defeated Vladislav Artemiev in the upper bracket, and Esipenko defeated Artemiev in the lower bracket to qualify. Photos: EWC

item.title: The Greater Seattle Chess Club to host its 50th meetup on August 12
item.description: It's an incredible thing in our country how different communities, especially stand-up comics, share a love for Chess. From figures like Samay Raina, Anirban Das Gupta, Vaibhav Sethia, and Biswa Kalyan Rath, the list goes on. Following these comics, on January 9, 2025, Vaibhav Bajaj, a stand-up comedian, took a step further and launched a Chess Club in Seattle named "The Greater Seattle Chess Club" (GSCC), building an open, inclusive space where tech engineers, casual blitz fans, and serious rated players gather weekly at different locations across Seattle. Photos: Vaibhav Bajaj.

item.title: Fabiano Caruana Starts with a Win at Sinquefield Cup 2026
item.description: The final Classical Event of the Grand Chess Tour, the 2026 Sinquefield Cup, returns to the Saint Louis Chess Club. On the Opening day, there was only 1 decisive result, where Caruana, Fabiano, defeated Jorden van Foreest with white pieces. The other 4 games, including R. Praggnanandhaa vs. Samuel Sevian, ended in a draw. The 2nd round will start at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photos: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Divya Deshmukh Beats Vaishali Rameshbabu in Round 1 of 6th Cairns Cup 2026
item.description: Divya Deshmukh defeated Vaishali Rameshbabu in the Opening Round of Cairns Cup 2026. Cairns Cup is one of the strongest women's super-tournaments in the world, and 3 Indian Players are taking part in it. Koneru Humpy started the event with a draw against Stavroula Tsolakidou. In another decisive result, Alice Lee defeated Alexandra Kosteniuk, and Tan Zhongyi won against Carissa Yip. The 2nd round will start at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photos: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Team Line-ups Confirmed for 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand
item.description: The International Chess Federation has officially published the team line-ups for the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad, to be held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, from September 15 to 27, 2026. Featuring 11 classical rounds following the opening ceremony on September 15, this edition will be the largest in chess history. A record-breaking 400 teams have been confirmed across two competitions: 208 in the Open section and 192 in the Women's event, surpassing the previous record of 380 teams set at Budapest 2024. Photo: FIDE

item.title: 11-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan crowned Britain’s youngest-ever Women’s champion
item.description: England’s 11-year-old prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan, another superstar-in-the-making, became Britain’s youngest-ever Women’s Chess Champion. Her only loss in the tournament was to Shreyas Royal in Round 6. In a tense, rapid-chess playoff between the top female players, Sivanandan defeated Ireland’s 14-year-old Trisha Kanyamarala, a hugely promising talent herself and the first Irishwoman to hold the WGM title. Photo: Yuri Krylov

item.title: Ural State Mining University wins inaugural FIDE World University Team Championship 2026
item.description: Ural State Mining University has been crowned champion of the inaugural FIDE World University Team Championship Finals, defeating Saint Louis University in Sunday’s final in Almaty. The final day of competition brought the championship down to its two decisive encounters: Ural State Mining University against Saint Louis University for the title and Kazakh National University of Sports against The University of Texas at Dallas for third place. Photos: FIDE

item.title: Pranav Anand Wins Brasov Grand Prix Classic 2026
item.description: GM Pranav Anand scored an unbeaten 7.5/9 to win the Brasov Grand Prix Classic 2026. Pranav and Top Seed Igor Kovalenko both scored 7.5, but better tiebreaks helped Pranav win the title. In the final round, Pranav defeated Henriquez Villagra Cristobal with white pieces. The tournament was organised in Brasov, Romania, at Hotel Aro Palace from 25th to 31st July 2026. The total prize fund was 36.000€, with the top three prizes being Lei 25000, 15000 and 1000 along with Trophies. Photos: Romanian Chess Grand Prix
